title: Research roundup: 7 cool science stories we almost missed
gist: A monthly roundup of seven under-covered August research results, spanning the identification of MoM-BH*-1 as a "black hole star" in JWST data, microbial upcycling of PET bottles into edible cookies, species-specific mosquito attraction chemistry, a single gene controlling avocado flowering sex, sound-powered microfliers, and a heat-driven elastocaloric cooling system using nickel-titanium films. Several items have direct commercial adjacency in agriculture, cooling, and vector control.

themes.theme: Black hole stars in JWST data

insights.claim: Astronomers concluded that MoM-BH*-1, one of hundreds of mysterious "little red dots" found in James Webb Space Telescope datasets in 2024, is a "black hole star": a roughly 100-solar-mass central black hole wrapped in a dense hydrogen cocoon the size of our solar system.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A new object class emerging from JWST archival data underlines that the telescope's science return is still compounding years after launch.

insights.claim: The identification rested on the deepest Balmer break ever observed combined with a spectrum showing no metals or elements other than hydrogen and helium, plus brightness roughly 100 billion times that of a star that only an actively accreting black hole could produce.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: The reasoning chain — anomalous spectrum, then simulation to identify the only physically possible source — is a template for how AI-era archival astronomy will generate new object classes.
insights.locator: They described this new object in detail

insights.claim: Two more black hole stars have already been identified since the first, and astronomers hope the class will explain how supermassive black holes formed so soon after the Big Bang.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A rapidly growing sample suggests this becomes a mainstream research line, sustaining demand for JWST-class observing time and follow-up instruments.

insights.claim: Researchers at Southern Illinois University led by Lahiru Jayakody programmed yeast strains to convert polyethylene terephthalate from beverage bottles into proteins, vitamins and flavorings, then extruded the result through a 3D printer into edible cookies they call µBites.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: PET waste as a food feedstock would create an entirely new offtake market for plastic recyclate; the enabling step is a proprietary high-temperature, high-pressure depolymerization process.

insights.claim: The µBites team has not yet run human taste tests, and subjects said only that the cookies smell delicious and that they would eat them in a situation with very limited food options — a weak endorsement the author explicitly flags.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: The target market is captive-consumption environments — deep-space missions, submarines, Moon or Mars colonies — not consumer food, which caps near-term addressable demand.
insights.quote: That’s not quite a ringing endorsement, but it’s a start.

insights.claim: Oceanographer John Spiesberger traced anomalous whale-call sound speeds ranging from 1,000 to 3,000 meters per second — against a seawater standard of about 1,500 — to temporal interference between a direct signal and its surface echo rather than to a software bug.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A systematic error mode in acoustic time-of-arrival localization matters for any underwater tracking or sonar-derived positioning system, not just whale research.

insights.claim: In temporal interference the signal's strongest peak can appear to travel faster than light while the encoded information still obeys special relativity, so no physics is violated.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Useful mental model: peak velocity and information velocity are different quantities, a distinction that recurs in signal-processing and communications engineering claims.

insights.claim: A study led by Matthew DeGennaro of Florida International University exposing 119 human volunteers to three mosquito species found each species decodes human scent differently: Aedes aegypti preferred men, Aedes albopictus was drawn to elevated ketones and plant-like volatiles, and Culex quinquefasciatus selected hosts by skin microbiome.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Species-specific attraction chemistry is the scientific basis for species-specific repellents and region-targeted vector-control strategies — a differentiated product line for consumer and public-health chemical makers.

insights.claim: UC Davis scientists identified a single gene, SDMYB, that determines whether an avocado tree follows the A-type schedule (female flowers in the morning, male in the afternoon) or the reciprocal B-type pattern, with A-types carrying one dominant and one recessive allele and B-types two recessive copies.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: A genetic marker resolves a century-old agronomic mystery and creates a testable trait — the kind of finding that flows into seed and nursery IP.
insights.locator: Avocados switch sex several times a day

insights.claim: Growers can now genotype avocado trees at the seedling stage to determine A-type or B-type and stagger plantings for pollen exchange, instead of waiting the 10 to 15 years after planting it previously took for a tree to flower and reveal its type.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Collapsing a 10-15 year feedback loop to a seedling test materially changes orchard capital planning and yield risk for avocado producers.
insights.locator: In fact, the same two versions were found

insights.claim: The same two gene versions appear in 26 other related tree species, indicating the flowering-sex mechanism is not confined to avocados.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Cross-species conservation broadens the potential commercial footprint of the marker beyond a single crop.
insights.locator: In fact, the same two versions were found

insights.claim: EPFL researchers converted sound into propulsive force by embedding fabricated hollow cavities in 3D-printed devices, exploiting Helmholtz resonance so that oscillating air forced out of the cavities generates thrust.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Untethered, battery-free actuation for microscale robots removes the dominant power-and-weight constraint in that category.

insights.claim: By tuning three cavities to different frequencies, the EPFL team steered miniature boats simply by changing the speaker frequency, and built 3D-printed microfliers with ultrasonic-tuned cavities that generate upward thrust or aerodynamic lift.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Frequency-multiplexed control means one external emitter can address many degrees of freedom, a cheap alternative to onboard control electronics.

insights.claim: Researchers coupled two ultra-thin nickel-titanium films so that the first shrinks when heated — converting thermal energy into mechanical work without an electric motor — and transfers that work to the second film, whose reversible crystal-structure change generates cold.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Removing the electrically driven actuator is the barrier that has kept elastocaloric cooling from competing with vapor-compression; this is the enabling step.

insights.claim: The approach makes solid-state cooling drivable by waste heat and solar energy, with the authors pointing to cooling computer processors using their own waste heat and cooling car electronics from drivetrain waste heat as target applications.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Waste-heat-driven processor cooling would directly attack data center thermal and power budgets, the binding constraint on AI compute buildout.
insights.locator: This makes it possible to drive solid-state cooling

insights.claim: The elastocaloric result is currently only a feasibility demonstration, with the next step being to connect multiple films to increase cooling capacity before any scale-up is possible.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Capacity scaling is unproven, so treat commercial timelines for heat-driven solid-state cooling as long-dated optionality rather than a near-term threat to compressor incumbents.
insights.quote: Thus far, it is just a demonstration of the feasibility of the approach
insights.locator: This makes it possible to drive solid-state cooling
